doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: First reading of 'Mercy' at Lennie's on the Turnpike; Buddy Rich's time feel
summary: Buddy Rich passed out the chart at a packed Sunday show; Wilson ties his time sense to Rich and Makoto Ozone.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Were you there when they first read it?

I sure was. At the end of the week they do the Sunday afternoon show, You know what that means, they’ll play one set at 2. And I brought all the charts out. It was cold, it was one of those winter days. I had a long scarf around me and all that sort of thing and I knew I better have “Mercy” done. That’s the only one that really mattered to him at that point. And the place, Lennie’s on the Turnpike, Route 1 — I guess that would be Topsfield, and I walked into the door. The band is right here, all playing and he’s over near the wall over there. And he just — he can see me coming in the door, the door’s right there. The place is standing room only I mean it is packed, the Sunday session, right? And he yelled over, “You’ve got ‘Mercy’?” I said, “Yeah.” “Pass it out.” And he passed it out. Yup. And I said, “You’ve got to be careful, there’s a drum break for you that is one bar longer than you think. So you’re going to have to think about that.” And then two, three, four bang. Now you’ve got to remember I got many of those guys like Richie Cole and, you know, they were all friends of mine and had been with me with the Dues Band. So I got them on the band in the first place so they knew me and there was no problem there. And also I liked Buddy Rich. Buddy and I were friends and that was I guess my time sense is Buddy Rich’s time sense. And it goes back to that stupid drumset that I had as a 10-year-old playing to Buddy Rich, of all things, Opus #1, “Sunny Side of the Street” and all those things that he did for Tommy. The time feel was all Buddy and that force has been with me. It still is. Makoto used to say to me, he said, “You know why we play so well together?” And I looked over and I said, “Yes I do.” And he looked at me and we both said together, “Buddy Rich.” We locked in. In fact Makoto and I toured around for about three years because of that record we made.
What was the reaction to the first reading of “Mercy Mercy” at Lennie’s on the Turnpike?
Yup. I’m certainly going well I’ll be damned. Yup. That’s what happened.
I’ve actually got a picture of me rehearsing his band. Of course I loved it. That’s where I live.
